case_name: Nokia 6230 — Norwegian WAP Cache Forensic Analysis (2004)
source_dataset: Champlain College Digital Forensics Challenge — Mobile Phone Corpus
description: Forensic image of Nokia 6230 internal flash memory (file Rh-12_352953003422072-bilder.bin). IMEI 352953003422072. Contains WAP browser cache and picture storage from a Norwegian user, June–August 2004. User browsed Norwegian-language WAP sites: Yahoo Norway (no.wap.yahoo.com), NRK Norwegian Broadcasting (wap.nrk.no), TV2 (tv2.by.com), Aftenposten newspaper, Telenor Mobile WAP portal, Nordialog telecom. Two MMS sessions via internal Telenor MMSC (10.250.31.100:10021) with unique session tokens. WML and GIF content cached. SSL certificates from VeriSign and Thawte present. Shannon entropy 5.21 bits/byte (SUSPICIOUS range, consistent with compressed WAP cache). No anomalous behavior detected — normal Norwegian mobile user activity in summer 2004.
devil_advocate: N/A — verdict is NOISE, refutation protocol not required.

artifacts.description: Shannon entropy 5.2114 bits/byte on sampled content. SUSPICIOUS range per VIGIA thresholds (>5.0). However, this is fully explained by WAP cache content: HTTP response bodies are compressed binary GIF/JPEG images interleaved with plaintext WML. Mixed binary+text is structurally expected to produce entropy in 5.0-5.5 range. No encrypted payloads detected. No local entropy anomalies (hidden encrypted blocks) found. CAIE composite score 0.0479 (NOISE).

metadata.benign_explanation: Mixed binary (GIF/JPEG images) and plaintext (WML) in WAP cache produces entropy above pure-text baseline
